info.title: canopy private-server
info.description:
Admin/operator API for the canopy fleet manager. Requests are gated behind Tailscale auth; admin-only endpoints additionally check the caller is on the admin list.

Request bodies may be sent compressed, and this is recommended for large payloads: the server transparently decodes `Content-Encoding: gzip`, `br`, `deflate`, or `zstd`. The accepted encodings are also listed structurally in the `x-request-compression` extension.

post.summary: Add an email address to the admin allow-list.
post.description:
Grants admin access to the given email address. Has no effect if the
email is already an admin.

200.description: Admin added (idempotent).

post.summary: Remove an email address from the admin allow-list.
post.description:
Revokes admin access for the given email address. Has no effect if the
email was not an admin.

200.description: Admin removed (idempotent).

post.summary: List the admin allow-list.
post.description:
Returns the email addresses of every account currently granted admin
access to this API, in no particular order.

200.description: Admin emails.

post.summary: Allow this server to restore for the next 24 hours.
post.description:
Opens the server's restore window so an operator can run an ad-hoc
`bestool canopy restore` on it: while the window is open the device can mint
read-only restore credentials for its group's backup repository. The window
auto-expires after 24 hours; calling again re-arms it from now. Returns the
new window. Restores are gated behind this deliberate opt-in because they
grant read access to the group's entire backup history.

post.summary: Cancel a pending full-maintenance request.
post.description:
Clears the group's outstanding request for a one-off full maintenance
run. Cancelling when nothing is pending — or when the run has already
started — succeeds without effect. Returns the updated configuration.

post.summary: Cancel a pending one-off backup or restore request.
post.description:
Removes the pending request matching the given server, type, and
purpose. Cancelling when nothing is pending succeeds without effect.

post.summary: List a server's backup capabilities and their enabled state.
post.description:
Returns one entry per backup type the server has advertised, with its
enabled state, scheduling information, and recent run status. Empty if
the server hasn't advertised any capabilities yet.

post.summary: Remove a group's schedule and retention override for a backup type.
post.description:
The type reverts to inheriting the canopy-wide default schedule and
retention. Returns the updated configuration.

post.summary: Register a new external (bring-your-own-account) backup configuration.
post.description:
This only records the configuration, in a provisioning state; it does not
create the backup repository itself — call the `/backups/create_repo`
endpoint next. Returns 409 if the group already has a backup
configuration, or 404 if the group doesn't exist.

post.summary: Trigger (or retry) provisioning of a group's backup repository.
post.description:
Sets the configuration's status to provisioning and clears any previous
error, so provisioning is retried asynchronously; a failure surfaces in
the `last_init_error` field rather than in this call's response.
Idempotent — safe to call again while provisioning is already in
progress. Returns 409 if the repository is already ready.

post.summary: Onboard a group onto Canopy's shared-account backups.
post.description:
Use this for deployments that don't have their own AWS account. Canopy
generates a bucket name automatically, generates and stores the repository
passphrase, and marks the configuration as provisioning with shared
placement. The bucket and its access roles are provisioned asynchronously;
any failure surfaces in the `last_init_error` field rather than in this
call's response. Unlike the `/backups/create` and `/backups/upsert`
endpoints (used for bring-your-own-account setups), the caller does not
supply a bucket or role ARNs, and no bucket probe is performed. Returns
502 only if the server's secret storage isn't configured.

post.summary: Delete a group's backup configuration (decommission).
post.description:
The bucket and its existing backups are left untouched — object lock
prevents deletion — but this stops credential issuance for the group and
deletes the stored repository passphrase, which must not outlive its
configuration.

post.summary: Stop allowing this server to restore, immediately.
post.description:
Closes the server's restore window now, before its 24-hour expiry. Any
credentials already minted keep their (at most one hour) validity, but no
new restore credentials can be minted until an operator allows restores
again. Closing an already-closed window succeeds without effect.

post.summary: Get a group's backup configuration.
post.description:
Returns the full configuration and lifecycle state for a server group.
Returns `null` with a 200 status if the group has no backup configuration
yet; 404 only if the group itself doesn't exist.

post.summary:
List the effective schedule and retention for every backup type a group's
servers have declared support for (not just the ones currently enabled).
post.description:
A type with no scheduled interval still appears, with a null
`effective_interval`, since a manually run backup of that type is still
retained under its own policy.

post.summary: List all groups with a backup configuration.
post.description:
Returns one summary row per configured group: the bucket, how the
repository passphrase originated, the provisioning status, and the
last provisioning error if any.

post.summary: Inspect a bucket/prefix for the backup setup wizard.
post.description:
Assumes the maintenance role and reports what's there: empty, an existing
backup repository, other (non-backup) content, or inaccessible — plus
whether Canopy already has a configuration for this bucket and prefix.
Read-only; it never creates or modifies anything.

post.summary:
Issue a fresh recovery-verification challenge: a nonce encrypted to the
configured recovery recipients.
post.description:
The operator decrypts it offline to prove a private key is genuinely
held, then submits the plaintext to the `/backups/recovery_verify`
endpoint. Returns 502 if recovery recipients aren't configured on this
server.

post.summary: Get the disaster-recovery verification status.
post.description:
Reports the configured recovery recipients, when recovery was last
verified, and whether a fresh verification is due (either because a
year has passed or because the recipient set changed).

post.summary: Complete the recovery-verification ceremony.
post.description:
Checks that the submitted answer matches the outstanding challenge
issued by the `/backups/recovery_challenge` endpoint, then records the
verification against the current recipient set. Returns 400 if there's
no outstanding challenge, it has expired, or the answer is wrong.

post.summary:
Request an out-of-cycle full maintenance run for a group's backup
repository.
post.description:
It runs on the scheduler's next pass rather than waiting for its regular
staggered interval. Idempotent — re-requesting keeps the request pending.
Requires the repository to be ready; returns 409 otherwise.

post.summary: Request a one-off backup or restore for a server.
post.description:
Idempotent per server, type, and purpose — re-requesting refreshes the
existing pending request rather than creating a duplicate.

post.summary: The current restore-window state for a server.
post.description:
Reports until when the server may mint restore credentials for itself, or
`null` if restores are not currently allowed (never opened, or expired).

post.summary: Enable or disable a server's backup capability for one type.
post.description:
Disabled capabilities are excluded from scheduling and can't be issued
backup credentials, outside of explicit operator-requested runs.

post.summary: Set the schedule and retention override for one backup type of a group.
post.description:
A null interval means manual-only backups (no schedule). A specified
retention policy is validated against the organization's retention floor
and rejected with 400 if it falls below it, unless `allow_below_floor` is
set.

post.summary: Set the canopy-wide default schedule and retention for a backup type.
post.description:
A retention policy below the organization's retention floor is rejected
with 400, unless `allow_below_floor` is set.

post.summary: Get backup statistics for a group.
post.description:
Returns the group's cached repository stats, recent backup and
maintenance runs, pending one-off requests, and each member server's
declared backup capabilities.

post.summary: List the canopy-wide default schedule and retention for every backup type.
post.description: Groups inherit these defaults unless they set a per-group override.

post.summary: Update a group's mutable backup configuration fields.
post.description:
Currently only the region can be changed. Structural fields — bucket,
roles, mode — can only be set when the configuration is created;
schedule and retention are managed through the `/backups/set_schedule`
endpoint. Returns the updated configuration.

post.summary: Declaratively create or update a group's backup configuration.
post.description:
Registers or converges a group's backup configuration in a single
idempotent call, generating and storing the repository passphrase and (for
a new configuration) provisioning the repository automatically. Creating a
configuration only succeeds onto an empty, unclaimed bucket — a bucket
that already holds a backup repository or other content, or one that
can't be accessed, is rejected. Re-applying an existing configuration
reconciles the role ARNs and region to match the request; `bucket` and
`prefix` are immutable and any mismatch is rejected.

post.summary: Soft-delete a saved snippet.
post.description:
Marks the given snippet version as deleted; it stops appearing in the
snippet list, but the version itself (and the rest of its history)
isn't removed. Deleting one version doesn't affect any other version
in the same snippet's history.

200.description: Snippet soft-deleted.

post.summary: Resolve a snippet id to its latest version.
post.description:
Follows the version chain forward from the given id and returns the
newest id in that chain (the same id, if it's already the latest).
Useful for turning a stored or bookmarked snippet id into the id of
its current version.

200.description: The newest id in the supersedes chain rooted at the given id.

post.summary: Get a saved SQL snippet by id.
post.description:
Returns the full content of the given snippet version, including its
SQL text. The id doesn't have to be the current version — superseded
and deleted versions can still be fetched directly.

post.summary: List saved SQL snippets.
post.description:
Returns a page of the current snippets in the library — one entry per
snippet, showing only its latest, non-deleted version — ordered by
name, together with the total count.

post.summary: Save a SQL snippet.
post.description:
Creates a brand new snippet, or — when `supersedes` is set — a new
version that supersedes an existing one. The new version is recorded
under the caller's Tailscale identity. Returns the full content of the
newly created version.

post.summary: Check whether the caller is an admin.
post.description:
Reports `true` if the caller is authenticated and their identity is on
the admin allow-list, `false` otherwise — including when the caller is
not authenticated at all. This endpoint intentionally requires no
authentication of its own, since it exists so a client can check whether
to show admin-only controls before doing anything else.

200.description: `true` if the caller's Tailscale identity is an administrator (on the admin allow-list, or granted admin by the tailnet policy); `false` otherwise (including when no Tailscale identity is present).

post.summary: Get the configured public API base URL.
post.description:
Returns the base URL of the device-facing public API for this
deployment, or `null` if none is configured. Used by the operator UI to
build links out to device-facing resources.

200.description: Public-server URL, if configured.

post.summary: Get a ready-to-share link to the public server-versions page.
post.description:
Returns a full URL to the public server-versions status page, with its
access secret already embedded in the query string, so it can be shared
and opened directly without further configuration. Returns `null` if the
public API base URL or the server-versions secret is not configured.

200.description: Server-versions URL with embedded auth secret, if configured.

post.summary: Register an externally-generated public key as an active key on a device.
post.description:
Unlike the `provision_credential` endpoint, Canopy never generates or
sees a private key here — the operator supplies the public half of a
keypair they already hold. Returns 400 if the supplied value isn't a
valid public key, and 404 if the device doesn't exist.

post.summary: Attach a device to a Tailscale network node.
post.description:
Resolves the given identifier against the cached tailnet directory and
records the canonical node identity on the device. Returns the updated
device record, including its live tailnet snapshot when available.

404.description: Identifier does not resolve to a known tailnet node.

409.description: Another device already claims this node id.

503.description: Tailnet directory not configured or unreachable.

post.summary: Count how many times a device has connected.
post.description:
Returns the total number of connections recorded for the device, for
paginating its connection history.

post.summary: List a device's connection history, most recent first.
post.description:
Supports cursor-based pagination: pass the oldest entry from a previous
page as `before` to continue further back in time.

post.summary: Disable a single key so it can no longer authenticate.
Detach a device from its Tailscale network node.
post.description:
Returns the updated device record, with its tailnet identity cleared.
Returns 404 if the device doesn't exist.

post.summary: Disable every active key on a device, so none of them can authenticate.
post.description:
The keys stay in the device's history and can be re-enabled individually.
Any Tailscale identity attached to the device is untouched — detach it
separately.

post.summary: Look up a single device by id.
post.description:
Returns full device details: its identity and role, every key ever
registered on it, its most recent connection, and a live Tailscale
snapshot when available. Returns 404 if no device exists with that id.

post.summary: List servers a device was previously associated with, but no longer is.
post.description:
Useful for tracing a device's history when it has since been reassigned
or replaced on a different server.

post.summary: List the servers a device is currently associated with.
post.description:
Returns the servers this device is currently bound to (usually zero or
one), including reachability status and a best-effort display address
for each.

post.summary: List registered devices, paginated.
post.description:
Returns a page of the device registry, newest first, plus the total
count for rendering a pager. Every registered device is included,
whatever its role.

post.summary: Merge one device record into another.
post.description:
Combines keys, connections, and tailnet/server attachments onto the
target device and removes the source. Used to reconcile a device that
was auto-discovered via the tailnet directory with the device it
actually corresponds to, once that device authenticates with its own
key. Returns 409 if both devices independently hold a Tailscale
identity or a server attachment, since the merge can't decide which one
to keep.

409.description: Both source and target hold tailscale identity or a server attachment.

post.summary: Generate a new device credential and return the private key once.
post.description:
Generates a keypair, registers its public key as an active key on a new
or existing device at the chosen role, and returns the private key
encrypted under a freshly-generated passphrase. Canopy keeps only the
public key — the private key is never stored or logged after this
response. Returns 404 if `device_id` is given but doesn't match an
existing device.

post.summary: Re-enable a previously disabled device key.
post.description: The key can authenticate again immediately.

post.summary: Look up a Tailscale IP address, node id, or DNS name.
post.description:
Resolves the identifier against the live tailnet directory and returns
its canonical node identity if found. Useful for confirming what an
identifier resolves to before using it to attach a device.

503.description: Tailnet directory not configured or unreachable.

post.summary: Search for devices by key, name, IP address, or Tailscale identity.
post.description: Returns an empty list if the query is blank.

post.summary: Rename a device key, or clear its name.
post.description:
Sets the key's display name to the given value, or removes the name
when `null` is passed.

post.summary: Change the role a device is trusted at.
post.description: Immediately changes what the device is permitted to do system-wide.

post.summary: Decommission a check fleet-wide.
post.description:
Retires the (source, check): its state on every server is resolved and
it stops counting toward health, incidents, and source staleness. When
the source has no live checks left, its per-server staleness clears
too. If the check is ever reported again it returns pending review at
the warning ceiling.

200.description: Check decommissioned.

post.summary: List the check policy catalog.
post.description:
Returns every known (source, check) together with its current policy,
ordered by source then name. An entry exists for every check any
source has ever reported; new checks are added automatically the
first time they're seen, with a default policy pending review.

200.description: Catalog rows ordered by source then check_name.

post.summary: Sample real data available to a healthcheck's conditional rules.
post.description:
Fetches the most recent status report from any server that reported
the given check, and returns the fields a conditional rule could
reference for it. Useful for discovering what data is actually
available before writing a rule, and for previewing how a candidate
rule would evaluate. Returns a `null` sample if no server has ever
reported this check.

200.description: Sample payload or null if no server has reported this check yet.

post.summary: List all known tag keys.
post.description:
Returns the sorted, deduplicated set of tag keys used across every
server and server group in the fleet, including keys not present on
the sample returned by the sampling endpoint. Useful for discovering
which `tag.<key>` variables are available when writing a conditional
rule, even for tags the sampled server doesn't happen to carry.

200.description: Sorted, distinct tag keys.

post.summary: Update a check's policy.
post.description:
Sets the ceiling and escalation flag (and optionally notes) for the
given (source, check), and marks it as reviewed by the caller. Saving
with the same values as before still counts as a review, so an
operator can acknowledge a check without changing its policy.

200.description: Updated catalog row.

post.summary: Replace a check's documentation.
post.description:
Stores the markdown document presented alongside the check wherever
its state appears, and over MCP. Sending `null` or a blank document
clears it. Doesn't mark the policy as reviewed — documenting a check
is not the same as reviewing its grading.

200.description: Updated catalog row.

post.summary: Replace a check's conditional rules.
post.description:
Stores a new set of conditional rules for the given (source, check)
(or removes them, if `rules` is `null`), and marks the check as
reviewed by the caller. Returns 400 if `rules` doesn't parse as a
valid ladder — for example an unknown comparison operator, a
malformed variable reference, or an odd number of entries.

200.description: Updated catalog row.

post.summary: Add a note to an incident.
post.description:
Records a note authored by the calling operator and returns it. Requires
the caller to be on the admin allow-list. Responds 400 if the note body
is empty or whitespace-only.

post.summary: Delete an incident note.
post.description:
Permanently removes the note. Notes cannot be edited in place; to change
one, delete it and add a replacement. Requires the caller to be on the
admin allow-list.

post.summary: Get an incident with its contributing issues.
post.description:
Returns the incident and every issue that has contributed to it, each
with the times it joined and (where applicable) left the incident.
Responds 404 if the incident does not exist.

post.summary: List open incidents across all server groups.
post.description: Returns every incident that is currently open, fleet-wide.

post.summary: List incidents for a server group.
post.description:
Returns the group's incidents. By default only open incidents are
returned; set `include_closed` to also include closed ones.

post.summary: List incidents involving a server.
post.description:
Returns incidents that issues on the given server have contributed to.
By default only open incidents are returned; set `include_closed` to
also include closed ones.

post.summary: List notes on an incident.
post.description:
Returns notes written on the incident itself; notes on its contributing
issues are not included.

post.summary: Resolve an incident.
post.description:
Marks the incident resolved with the given reason, recording the calling
operator as the resolver. Returns the updated incident. Requires the
caller to be on the admin allow-list.

post.summary: Undo an incident's resolution.
post.description:
Clears the incident's resolved state (time, resolver, and reason).
Returns the updated incident. Requires the caller to be on the admin
allow-list.

post.summary: Add a note to an issue.
post.description:
Records the calling operator as the author. Returns 400 if the note
body is empty or whitespace-only.

post.summary: Permanently delete a note from an issue.
post.description:
The note is removed outright; there is no undo. Deleting a note that
doesn't exist succeeds without effect.

post.summary: List issues across all servers, with optional filtering.
post.description:
Returns the most relevant issues fleet-wide, matching the given filters.
By default only currently active issues are returned; pass
`activeOnly: false` to also see resolved and inactive ones.

post.summary: List issues raised by a specific device.
post.description:
Returns the issues that the given device reported, most relevant
first. By default only currently active issues are returned; pass
`active_only: false` to also see resolved and inactive ones.

post.summary: List issues raised against a specific server.
post.description:
Returns the issues recorded against the given server, most relevant
first. By default only currently active issues are returned; pass
`active_only: false` to also see resolved and inactive ones.

post.summary: List the notes left on a specific issue.
post.description:
Returns the issue's notes, most recent first, each with its author and
creation time.

post.summary: Mark an issue as resolved.
post.description:
Records the calling operator as the resolver along with the given
reason, and returns the updated issue.

post.summary: Snooze an issue until a given time.
post.description:
A snoozed issue stops demanding attention until the given time, after
which it surfaces again on its own. Returns the updated issue.

post.summary: Manually raise (or clear) a condition against a server.
post.description:
Finds or creates an issue keyed by the server and the given `ref`
under the `manual` source, grades the chosen result through the
condition's catalog policy, and returns the resulting issue. Returns
400 if `ref` is empty or if `description` contains a newline.

post.summary: Undo a previous resolution, marking an issue as unresolved again.
post.description:
Clears the resolution timestamp, resolver, and reason, and returns the
updated issue.

post.summary: Clear a snooze on an issue.
post.description:
Makes a previously snoozed issue demand attention again immediately,
without waiting for its snooze time to pass. Returns the updated issue.

post.summary: List MCP access tokens.
post.description:
Returns every access token that has ever been minted, newest first,
including ones that have since been revoked — this is the full history
view. Token secrets are never included, only metadata about each token.

200.description: All MCP access tokens, newest first, revoked included.

post.summary: Mint a new MCP access token.
post.description:
Creates a new bearer token that can be used to authenticate against the
public MCP endpoint, and returns its metadata together with the
plaintext secret. The secret appears only in this response and cannot be
retrieved again afterwards, so it must be copied out immediately. Tokens
are valid for one year from minting. Returns 400 if the supplied name is
empty or only whitespace.

200.description: Freshly minted token; the secret in this response is shown once.

post.summary: Revoke an MCP access token.
post.description:
Immediately invalidates the token with the given id so it can no longer
authenticate. Revoking an already-revoked token succeeds without doing
anything further. Returns 404 if no token with that id exists.

200.description: Token revoked (idempotent).

post.summary: List recent restore activity for a group.
post.description:
Returns up to the 50 most recent restore-health reports submitted by
consumers for the given server group, plus restores inferred from credential
issuances that never reported (in flight, or terminated without a report).
Each reported check records whether a backup snapshot restored successfully
and whether the resulting replica was healthy — the strongest available
signal that the group's backups are actually restorable. Reported checks
carry a Canopy-measured duration (issuance → report).

post.summary: List restore consumers and their advertised intents.
post.description:
Returns every device with the backup-restore role, together with the
restore intents it currently advertises (each with its description,
semantics flags, and parameter schema). Use this to discover which
consumers and intents a declaration can target and which parameters each
intent accepts. Defaults of `duration` and `bytes` parameters are
formatted as human-unit strings (e.g. `2h`, `20Gi`).

post.summary: Declare a managed restore replica.
post.description:
Creates a declaration instructing the chosen consumer to maintain a
restored replica of the given backup type for the given intent, and
records the calling operator as its creator. The overdue bound is a
human-friendly duration string (e.g. `2h 30m`); `duration` and `bytes`
parameter values likewise accept human-unit strings (e.g. `20Gi`), which
are resolved to raw seconds/bytes before validation against the consumer's
advertised schema for the intent and stored raw. If the intent is not
currently advertised, the values are accepted as-is and the declaration is
created with a gap. Requires the caller to be on the admin allow-list.
Responds 400 if the overdue bound or a parameter value fails to parse or
validate, and 409 if a matching declaration already exists.

post.summary: Delete a restore replica declaration.
post.description:
Removes the declaration: the consumer stops being asked to maintain the
replica and loses the backup access the declaration granted. Any active
restore-verification alert for the declaration's scope is recovered, since
nothing tracks that scope any more. Requires the caller to be on the admin
allow-list. Responds 404 if the declaration does not exist.

post.summary: List restore replica declarations for a group.
post.description:
Returns every declaration scoped to the given server group, with each
consumer's display name resolved and the `gap` flag computed against the
intents the consumer currently advertises.

post.summary: Update a restore replica declaration.
post.description:
Replaces every field, including scope: the consumer, group, server,
backup type, and intent can be retargeted in the same call as the name,
overdue bound, parameter values, and enabled flag. The overdue bound and
`duration`/`bytes` parameter values accept human-unit strings (e.g.
`2h 30m`, `20Gi`), resolved to raw seconds/bytes and validated against the
*new* consumer+intent's advertised parameter schema; as with `create`, an
intent the new consumer doesn't currently advertise is accepted and the
values pass through unvalidated, leaving the declaration with a gap. If
the scope changes, any active restore-verification alert for the
declaration's old scope is recovered. Requires the caller to be on the
admin allow-list. Responds 400 if the overdue bound or a parameter value
fails to parse or validate, 404 if the declaration does not exist, and 409
if the new scope collides with another declaration.

409.description: The new scope collides with another declaration.

post.summary: List currently-alerting self-alerts.
post.description:
Returns self-alerts whose underlying condition is still ongoing and
that have not been marked resolved by an operator. This is the feed
meant for a live alert banner; see the full listing endpoint for
complete history including recovered and resolved alerts.

200.description: Currently-alerting self-alerts (active and not operator-resolved), for the banner.

post.summary: List self-alerts.
post.description:
Returns self-alerts ordered by most recent activity first, including
ones that have since recovered on their own or been resolved by an
operator. Use the "active" endpoint instead for just the ones currently
alerting.

200.description: Self-alerts, newest activity first, recovered/resolved included.

post.summary: Mark a self-alert as resolved.
post.description:
Records that an operator has resolved the given self-alert. Returns 404
if no self-alert with that id exists.

200.description: Alert marked operator-resolved.

post.summary: Create a server group.
post.description:
Creates a new, empty server group and returns it. Requires the caller to
be on the admin allow-list. Responds 400 if the request is invalid.

post.summary: Archive a server group.
post.description:
Soft-deletes the group: it disappears from live listings but is kept and
can be restored later. Requires the caller to be on the admin allow-list.
Responds 409 if the group still has live member servers; move or archive
those first.

post.summary: Get a server group with its members.
post.description:
Returns the group, its member servers (sorted by name, with current status
and display host), and the group's effective billing labels. Responds 404
if no group exists with the given identifier.

post.summary: List all live server groups.
post.description:
Returns every non-archived server group, including its name, notes, tags,
Slack notification delay, and effective version information. The request
body is ignored; send an empty JSON object.

post.summary: List archived server groups.
post.description:
Returns every group that has been archived (soft-deleted) and can be
restored. The request body is ignored; send an empty JSON object.

post.summary: Restore an archived server group.
post.description:
Un-archives a previously deleted group so it reappears in live listings.
Requires the caller to be on the admin allow-list. Responds 404 if the
group does not exist.

post.summary: Search live server groups.
post.description: Returns non-archived groups matching the free-text query.

post.summary: Count live servers per group.
post.description:
Returns one entry per server group that has at least one live
(non-archived) member server. Groups with no live members are omitted, so
treat a missing entry as a count of zero. The request body is ignored;
send an empty JSON object.

post.summary: Update a server group.
post.description:
Applies a partial update: only the fields present in `data` (name, notes,
tags, Slack notification delay) are changed. Returns the updated group.
Requires the caller to be on the admin allow-list. Responds 404 if the
group does not exist and 400 if the request is invalid.

post.summary: Attach a device to a server via a Tailscale identifier.
post.description:
Resolves the identifier to a tailnet node, finds the device already
attached to that node or creates a new one for it, and binds that device
to the server. Useful when a server has no device yet (e.g. an
operator-imported server that hasn't reported in) and should be bound to
a tailnet node directly. Returns 409 if the resolved device is already
attached to another live server — detach it there first.

200.description: Device id newly attached to the server.

404.description: Identifier does not resolve to a known tailnet node.

409.description: The resolved device is already attached to another server.

503.description: Tailnet directory not configured or unreachable.

post.summary: Create a new server.
post.description:
Creates the server record, optionally pre-bound to a Tailscale device
via `tailscale_identifier`, either ungrouped or in the given group.

200.description: New server id.

post.summary: Archive (soft-delete) a server.
post.description:
Releases and demotes its device. Archived servers no longer appear in
regular listings but can be restored later.

post.summary: Get the enrollment state of a server.
post.description:
Reports whether the server has completed enrollment, and whether an
enrollment token is currently outstanding (issue and expiry times only —
the token itself is never revealed).

post.summary: Get full detail for a server.
post.description:
Returns the server's record, its bound device (if any), its most recent
status report, current reachability/health, its group (if any) together
with sibling servers in the same group, and the group's billing labels.
Returns 404 if no server exists with that id.

post.summary: Get a server's basic record.
post.description:
Returns identity, classification, and configuration for a single server,
including its group name where applicable. Does not include current
reachability/health or device/group detail — use the detail endpoint for
that. Returns 404 if no server exists with that id.

post.summary: Get a server's display name.
post.description:
Returns the server's name if set, else its stored host, else its id —
always a non-empty string suitable for display. Returns 404 if no server
exists with that id.

post.summary: List archived (soft-deleted) servers.
post.description:
Each entry has `archived: true` and includes current reachability/health.
Archived servers can be brought back with the restore endpoint.

post.summary: List servers, optionally filtered by kind, paginated.
post.description:
Returns a page of servers plus the total matching count. Entries include
their group name where applicable, but not current reachability/health —
use the detail endpoint for that.

post.summary: List servers that don't belong to any group.
post.description:
Returns a page of ungrouped servers, each with current
reachability/health, plus the total count of ungrouped servers.

post.summary: Mint (or reissue) an enrollment ticket for a server.
post.description:
Creates a fresh enrollment token and returns it wrapped in a
passphrase-encrypted ticket the operator runs through bestool on the
enrolling machine, plus the 4-word passphrase that decrypts it. The
plaintext token lives only inside the encrypted ticket; reissuing
invalidates any prior token. Fails if the server is archived.

post.summary: Un-archive a server.
post.description:
Restores a previously archived server to regular listings. Its machine
must re-enroll afterwards to rebind a device. Restoring a server that
isn't archived has no effect.

post.summary: Revoke any outstanding enrollment ticket for a server.
post.description:
Use this when a ticket was issued by mistake or is no longer needed.
Afterwards, the enrollment status endpoint reports no outstanding token,
and the revoked ticket can no longer be used to enroll.

post.summary: Update a server's fields.
post.description:
Applies a partial update — only the fields present in `data` are
changed. Moving a previously-ungrouped server into a group, or toggling
`is_monitored`, re-evaluates the server's open issues so incidents catch
up with the new state. Returns 400 if the update is rejected (e.g. an
invalid host value).

post.summary: List group-scoped silences for a server group.
post.description:
Returns every (source, ref) pair currently silenced for this server
group — applying to every server in the group — most recently created
first.

post.summary: List server-scoped silences for a server.
post.description:
Returns every (source, ref) pair currently silenced specifically for
this server, most recently created first. Doesn't include silences
applied at the server's group level.

post.summary: Silence an issue on a server group.
post.description:
Suppresses alerting for the given (source, ref) pair across every
server in this group: matching issues keep being recorded, but stop
counting toward opening or extending an incident. Idempotent —
silencing a pair that's already silenced leaves the original entry,
including who created it and when, unchanged. Requires admin access.
Returns 400 if the request is invalid, for example if it references a
server group that doesn't exist.

post.summary: Silence an issue on a server.
post.description:
Suppresses alerting for the given (source, ref) pair on this server:
matching issues keep being recorded, but stop counting toward opening
or extending an incident. Idempotent — silencing a pair that's already
silenced leaves the original entry, including who created it and when,
unchanged. Requires admin access. Returns 400 if the request is
invalid, for example if it references a server that doesn't exist.

post.summary: Unsilence an issue on a server group.
post.description:
Removes a group-scoped silence for the given (source, ref) pair, if
one exists. Removing a silence that isn't there is not an error.
Requires admin access.

post.summary: Unsilence an issue on a server.
post.description:
Removes a server-scoped silence for the given (source, ref) pair, if
one exists. Removing a silence that isn't there is not an error.
Requires admin access.

post.summary: Run a query in the read-only SQL playground.
post.description:
The query runs inside an explicit read-only transaction — Postgres
rejects write statements within it — and the transaction is always
rolled back afterwards regardless of the outcome, so nothing it does
can be committed. Execution is capped at 60 seconds; a query that runs
longer is aborted and reported as an error. The query text is recorded
to the shared query history under the caller's identity before it
runs, even if execution subsequently fails.

Returns an error if the read-only SQL playground isn't configured on
this server, or if the query fails, times out, or can't be recorded to
history.

post.summary: Get the caller's most recently run playground query.
post.description:
Returns the SQL text of the last query the caller executed in the SQL
playground, or `null` if they haven't run one yet.

200.description: The caller's most recent SQL playground query, if any.

post.summary: List the shared history of SQL playground queries.
post.description:
Returns a page of every query run by any user in the SQL playground,
most recent first, together with the total number of entries.

post.summary: Check whether the read-only SQL playground is enabled.
post.description:
Returns `true` if this server is configured with a read-only database
connection to run playground queries against, `false` otherwise. Does
not require authentication.

200.description: Whether the read-only SQL playground is configured.

post.summary: List the servers whose check state reports one (source, check).
post.description:
Everything the per-healthcheck page needs: the catalog's configured
policy for the (source, check) (if any) plus every live server's
current state for it — the real-time picture, with each degraded row
carrying `failing_since` (the start of its current degradation
streak). This is the data behind the `/healthchecks/:source/:check`
"who's affected" page, which doubles as an operator TODO list and as
a way to correlate servers sharing the same issue during a
fleet-wide incident.

200.description: The check's catalog policy and the servers currently reporting it.

post.summary: Get a status card for a server group.
post.description:
Returns the group's identity, its headline version and how far behind
the latest published release that version is, and a per-member summary
(up/down state, health, connected operators, rank, kind) for every
server in the group. Returns 404 if the group doesn't exist.

post.summary: List server group ids, bucketed by rank.
post.description:
Each group is bucketed under the highest rank held by any of its member
servers (production outranks clone, which outranks demo, then test,
then dev). Groups whose members are all unranked are omitted entirely.
Within each rank bucket, groups are ordered alphabetically by name.

200.description: Server group IDs grouped by highest-ranked member's rank.

propertyNames.description: The environment tier of a server, from `production` down to `dev`.

post.summary: Get a server's status as of a point in time.
post.description:
Returns the most recent status push at or before `at` (or the latest
push overall, if `at` is omitted), enriched with version distance,
minimum browser version, connected operators, and per-check severities.
Returns `null` in the response body if the server has no recorded
status.

post.summary: Get a fleet-wide summary of software versions running in production.
post.description:
Looks at the most recent status reported by every server ranked as
production (within the last 7 days) and returns the range of versions
seen, the distinct release lines, and every distinct exact version.

post.summary:
Record a new known issue affecting a version's release line, starting
from the given version's exact patch.
post.description: Returns 400 if the description is empty or whitespace-only.

post.summary: Create a new artifact tied to an exact version.
post.description:
Registers a download of the given type and platform against the
version, and returns the created artifact.

post.summary: Permanently delete an artifact.
post.description:
The artifact record is removed outright; the file it pointed to is not
touched. There is no undo.

post.summary: List all versions, grouped by release line.
post.description:
Returns every version, including drafts, grouped by major.minor release
line and ordered newest release line first. Each group includes a
readiness flag reflecting whether its latest published patch has any
unresolved known issues.

post.summary: List the downloadable artifacts available for a version.
post.description:
Returns one entry per artifact type/platform combination actually
served for this version, whether tied to the exact version or matched
via a version range pattern. Returns 404 if the version doesn't exist.

post.summary: Get full details for a single version.
post.description:
Returns the version's changelog, minimum browser version requirement,
whether it's the latest patch in its release line, other versions in
the same release line, its readiness, and its full known-issue history.
Returns 404 if the version doesn't exist.

post.summary: List known issues for a version's release line.
post.description:
Returns every known issue ever raised against the major.minor release
line the given version belongs to, resolved or not. Returns 404 if the
version doesn't exist.

post.summary: Mark a known issue as resolved as of a given fix version.
post.description:
Returns 400 if the resolution message is empty or whitespace-only.
Returns 404 if the known issue doesn't exist, is already resolved, or
if `fix_version` isn't in the same release line as the issue or isn't
strictly above its earliest affected patch.

post.summary: Update an existing artifact's type, platform, and download URL.
post.description:
All three fields are replaced with the supplied values; the artifact's
version association is unchanged.

post.summary: Replace a version's changelog text.
post.description:
Overwrites the changelog of the version identified by its exact
version string. Updating a version that doesn't exist succeeds
without effect.

post.summary: Change a version's publication status.
post.description:
Returns 400 if the change would move a published version back to draft
while it isn't the latest published patch in its release line — older
published patches can't be un-published out from under a newer one.

result, the escalation flag, plus optional conditional rules that can
grade a given report differently.

ceiling.description:
The maximum effective result for this check when no conditional
rule (see `rules`) overrides it: an observed result more urgent
than the ceiling grades down to it. One of `failed`, `warning`,
`passed`, or `skipped` (`skipped` also tells the reporting source
it may stop running the check).

decommissioned_at.description:
When this check was decommissioned, if it has been. A decommissioned
check contributes to nothing until it is reported again. `null` while
live.

documentation.description:
Operator-authored documentation for this check: a single markdown
document. By convention it covers what the check observes, what
each result means, and hints for solving a failure, but no
structure is enforced. `null` when nobody has documented it yet.

escalates.description:
Whether an effective failure of this check notifies immediately,
bypassing the incident grace period.

first_seen.description:
When this check was first reported and this policy entry was
created.

last_seen.description:
When this check was most recently reported on any server across the
fleet. `null` until liveness has been reconciled since it first
appeared. A check quiet for long enough is a decommissioning
candidate.

reviewed_at.description:
When an operator last reviewed or updated this policy. `null` if
it has never been reviewed.

reviewed_by.description:
The operator who last reviewed this policy. `null` if it has
never been reviewed.

rule_count.description:
Number of condition/result branches in `rules`; `0` when
`rules` is `null` or couldn't be parsed. Lets a caller tell
whether conditional rules exist without parsing `rules` itself.

rules.description:
Conditional rules that can grade a report to a different result
than the ceiling would — in any direction — depending on the
check's own fields, the surrounding status report, or the
reporting server's tags. `null` means no conditional rules are
configured, and the ceiling always applies.

When present, this is a single-key object shaped like
`{"if": [condition_1, result_1, condition_2, result_2, ...]}`.
Conditions are tried in order, and the result paired with the
first matching condition is used; if none match, the observed
result capped at the ceiling is used instead. There's no explicit
"else" branch — the ceiling fallback plays that role — so the
array must have an even number of entries and at least one pair.

Each condition is a single-key object naming a comparison
operator — one of `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, or `in_range`
— whose value is a two-element array: a variable reference and a
value to compare it against. A variable reference has the shape
`{"var": "<namespace>.<field>"}`, where `<namespace>` is one of
`check` (a field on the failing check itself), `status` (a
top-level field on the status report that contained it), or
`tag` (a tag on the reporting server, merged with its group's
tags). `in_range` compares a version-like string against a
semantic version range (e.g. `">=1.2.0 <2.0.0"`). If the named
variable isn't present in the data being evaluated, the condition
doesn't match. A `rules` value that doesn't parse into this shape
is treated the same as `null` (no conditional rules).

source.description: The source that reports this check.

updated_at.description: When this policy was last modified.

Older reports may send a plain pass/fail flag instead of one of these
outcomes; when that happens a passing flag is treated as `passed` and a
failing flag as `failed`.

IncidentData.description:
An operational incident: a group-scoped roll-up of related issues.

An incident opens when an issue on a server in the group crosses the
severity threshold, gathers further contributing issues while open, and
closes automatically once the last serious contributor clears. Operators
can additionally mark an incident resolved with a reason.

closed_at.description:
When the incident closed (all serious contributing issues cleared);
null while the incident is still open.

created_at.description: When the incident record was created.

issue_count.description: Number of distinct issues that have ever contributed to the incident.

lingering_since.description:
When set, the incident is lingering: its last effective failure
recovered at this time, and the incident stays open for the group's
linger window in case the failure comes back (which would continue
this incident rather than open a new one). Null while a failure is
live, and always null on a closed incident. Lets a client
distinguish "open and failing" from "open but currently recovered".

note_count.description:
Combined count of notes on the incident itself plus notes on all its
contributing issues.

notification_held_until.description:
When set, the "incident opened" Slack notification is being held
until this time by the group's notification delay (which suppresses
flapping); an incident that resolves before then never notifies.
Null once the notification has been sent, cancelled, or given up on.
Lets a client distinguish "open but quietly held" from "open and
operators have been notified".

resolved_at.description:
When an operator marked the incident resolved; null if it has not
been resolved.

resolved_by.description: Login of the operator who resolved the incident, if resolved.

resolved_by_name.description: Display name of the resolving operator, if known.

resolved_by_pic.description: Avatar URL of the resolving operator, if known.

resolved_reason.description:
Reason given when resolving: one of `fixed`, `wont_fix`, `expected`,
`duplicate`, or `flapping`.

server_group_id.description:
Identifier of the server group the incident belongs to, or null for
a canopy-wide incident (aggregating canopy's self-alerts).

server_group_name.description:
Display name of the group this incident rolls up to — `Canopy` for
a canopy-wide incident. Empty only if the group no longer exists,
which should not happen in normal operation.

updated_at.description: When the incident record was last modified.

One issue's involvement in an incident.

An issue joins an incident while it is actively contributing and leaves
when it stops (for example when it is resolved, snoozed, or silenced);
the same issue can join, leave, and rejoin over the incident's life.

joined_at.description: When the issue joined (started contributing to) the incident.

left_at.description:
When the issue left (stopped contributing to) the incident; null
while it is still contributing.

kind.description: The kind of deployment this server represents.

name.description: Operator-assigned name for the server, if any.

registered_at.description:

tags.description: Arbitrary operator-defined key/value labels attached to the server.

oneOf.description:

`integer` accepts any whole number, positive or negative; `boolean` is a

both directions with a read-only no-op). Optional; supplying it lets

Result of inspecting a bucket/prefix: what's currently stored there, and
whether Canopy already has a configuration for it.

already_configured.description:

error.description:

encountered while trying to access the bucket.

object_sample.description: A few example object keys found, when `state` is `other_content`.

What was found at the inspected location: empty, an existing backup
repository, other (non-backup) content, or inaccessible.

ProblemDetailsSchema.description:
Standard error response body, returned for every non-2xx response.

This follows the RFC 7807 "Problem Details" shape: a stable machine-readable
`type`, a short `title`, the repeated HTTP `status` code, and an optional
`detail` string with specifics of this particular occurrence.

detail.description:
Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the
problem, if any extra detail is available.

status.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated here for convenience.

title.description:
Short, human-readable summary of the problem type. Does not vary
between occurrences of the same `type`.

type.description:
A URI reference identifying the problem type. Stable across
occurrences of the same error, so callers can match on it.

ProvisionArgs.description: Request to mint a new device credential.

device_id.description:
Attach the new credential to this existing device instead of
creating a new one. When omitted, a new device is created at
`role`.

key_name.description: Display name for the new key. Defaults to "Provisioned key".

role.description: Role to trust the device at.

ProvisionedCredential.description:
The one-time result of provisioning a device credential. The plaintext
private key lives only inside `key_age_base64`; Canopy never persists it.

device_id.description: The device the credential was issued for.

filename.description: Suggested filename for the downloaded encrypted key.

fingerprint.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the stored public key, to correlate the
credential with the device's key list.

key_age_base64.description:
Base64 (standard) of the age-encrypted PKCS#8 PEM private key. Decrypt
with `passphrase` (e.g. `bestool crypto reveal`) to recover the PEM.

key_id.description: Unique identifier for the newly-created key record.

passphrase.description:
Freshly-generated passphrase that decrypts `key_age_base64`. Share it
out-of-band, on a separate channel from the file.

RecentRun.description:
One row of the recent-runs view: either a device-reported [`BackupRun`] or a
run inferred from a [`BackupCredentialIssuance`] that never matched a report.
Duration, when present, is Canopy-measured wall-clock — the interval from the
run's first credential issuance (its start) to its report (its end) — not a
client-reported figure.

at.description:
The row's effective time for sorting and display: `reported_at` when
reported, otherwise `started_at`.

bytes_uploaded.description: Bytes the device reported uploading, if any (reported runs only).

duration_seconds.description:
Canopy-measured run duration in seconds (report time minus first-issuance
time). `None` for an in-flight/unreported row or a run with no matching
issuance.

error.description: Error detail for a failed reported run, if any.

key.description:
Stable identity for UI keying: `run-<uuid>` for a reported run, or
`issuance-<id>` for an inferred attempt.

oneOf.description: The reported outcome; only present when `status` is `reported`.

purpose.description: Whether the run was a backup or a restore.

reported_at.description: When the device reported the run. `None` for an inferred (unreported) row.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes received from S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes received from S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes sent to S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes sent to S3 during the run, if tallied (reported runs only).

server_id.description: The server this run was for, if known.

snapshot_id.description:
Snapshot the run produced (backup) or used (restore), if any (reported
runs only).

snapshot_logical_bytes.description:
Logical size of the run's snapshot, if known (reported runs only). For
a backup this comes from repo inspection. For a restore it is resolved
from the backup run that produced the snapshot (matched by snapshot id),
falling back to inspection's backfill onto the restore run itself.

started_at.description:
When the run started, taken from its first matching credential issuance.
`None` when no issuance could be matched (e.g. a run predating issuance
recording).

status.description: Whether this row is reported, in-flight, or an unreported past attempt.

ciphertext_base64.description:
A single-use verification challenge encrypted to the recovery
recipients, base64-encoded. The operator decrypts this offline with a
held private key (any tool that supports the `age` encryption format)
and submits the decrypted plaintext to the `/backups/recovery_verify`
endpoint to prove the key is genuinely held.

recipients.description:
The recovery recipients (age public keys) this challenge was
encrypted to.

RecoveryStatusResponse.description:
Status of the disaster-recovery verification ceremony: whether recovery
is configured, and whether a fresh verification is due.

configured.description: Whether recovery recipients are configured on this server at all.

due.description: Whether a fresh verification ceremony is due.

last_verified_at.description: When the recovery ceremony was last completed successfully, if ever.

last_verified_recipients.description: The recipient set the last verification covered.

last_write_at.description: When the vault object was last successfully written by the backups pod.

last_write_bytes.description: Size (bytes) of the ciphertext from the last successful write.

recipients.description:
Fingerprints of the currently configured recovery recipients (age
public keys).

RecoveryVerifyArgs.description: Answer to an outstanding recovery-verification challenge.

answer.description:
The plaintext obtained by decrypting the challenge from the
`/backups/recovery_challenge` endpoint.

RecoveryVerifyResponse.description: Result of a successful recovery verification.

Another patch version within the same release line as a version being

Why this run is requested: `backup` to write new data, or `restore` to
read existing data.

server_id.description: The server to back up or restore.

ResolveIncidentArgs.description: Request to mark an incident resolved.

incident_id.description: Identifier of the incident to resolve.

reason.description: Why the incident is considered resolved.

ResolveKnownIssueArgs.description: Identifies a known issue and the version that fixes it.

fix_version.description:
Version string of the first patch that contains the fix. Must be in
the same release line as the issue's earliest affected patch, and
strictly above it.

known_issue_id.description: Id of the known issue to resolve.

resolution_message.description:
Explanation of how or where the issue was fixed. Must not be empty
or whitespace-only.

ResolveTailnetIdentifierArgs.description: A Tailscale identifier to resolve against the live tailnet directory.

identifier.description: A Tailscale IP address, node id, or DNS name to look up.

ResolveTailnetIdentifierResponse.description: Result of resolving a Tailscale identifier.

oneOf.description:
The resolved node's live details, or null if the identifier
didn't match any node in the tailnet.

ResolvedReason.description:
Reason an issue or incident was resolved by an operator.

Stored as text in Postgres, validated as this enum at the API layer.
Categories follow common operational practice (PagerDuty/Sentry/Opsgenie):

- `Fixed` — the underlying problem was addressed.
- `WontFix` — won't fix; not worth doing, or not actually a problem.
- `Expected` — known/expected behaviour (e.g. planned maintenance window).
- `Duplicate` — a duplicate of another issue.
- `Flapping` — too noisy; suppressed rather than fixed (often paired with
  a snooze).
- `Decommissioned` — the check itself was retired fleet-wide; its states
  are resolved as a side effect, not by an operator addressing them.

RestoreActivity.description:
One row of the restore-activity view: either a consumer-reported restore
health check, or a restore inferred from a credential issuance that never
reported (in flight, or terminated without a report). Mirrors the backup
recent-runs view on the restore side.

at.description:
Effective time for sorting/display: the report's observed time when
reported, otherwise the issuance start.

duration_seconds.description:
Canopy-measured restore duration in seconds (report received time minus
first-issuance time). `None` for an in-flight/unreported row or a check
with no matching issuance.

error.description: Error detail for a failed reported restore, if any.

health_details.description: Consumer-supplied health data, if any (reported checks only).

intent.description: The restore intent, when reported. Absent for inferred rows.

key.description:
Stable identity for UI keying: `check-<id>` for a reported check, or
`issuance-<id>` for an inferred restore.

observed_at.description:
When the consumer observed the restore result (client-reported); reported
checks only.

outcome.description: The restore outcome; only present for a reported check.

postgres_version.description: PostgreSQL version of the restored database, if reported.

replica_healthy.description: Whether the restored replica came up healthy; only for a reported check.

reported_at.description: When the consumer's report was received. `None` for an inferred row.

s3_received_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes received from S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_received_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes received from S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_sent_payload_bytes.description: Payload bytes sent to S3 during the restore, if reported.

s3_sent_raw_bytes.description: Raw bytes sent to S3 during the restore, if reported.

server_id.description:
The server the restore is for, when reported. Absent for inferred rows
(the issuance is minted per group+type, not per server).

snapshot_id.description: The snapshot that was restored, if reported.

started_at.description:
When the restore started, taken from its matching credential issuance.
`None` when no issuance could be matched.

status.description: Reported, in-flight, or an unreported terminated restore.

RestoreConsumerView.description:
A restore consumer and the restore intents it currently advertises.

A restore consumer is a device with the `backup-restore` role: an agent
that restores backups onto standby replicas. Each advertised intent
carries a description, semantics flags, and a parameter schema, which
together determine what declarations can be created for the consumer and
what parameters they accept.

intents.description: The intents the consumer currently advertises support for.

name.description: Display name of the consumer device, if known.

RestoreReplicaView.description:
A managed-restore declaration, as shown to operators.

A declaration instructs a restore consumer to maintain a restored replica
of a backup, for a given purpose (intent). It also grants the consumer
read access to the covered backups while it is enabled.

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device the declaration is assigned to.

consumer_name.description: Display name of the consumer device, if known.

created_by.description: Login of the operator who created the declaration, if recorded.

enabled.description:
Whether the declaration is active. Disabled declarations are not
dispatched to the consumer and grant no backup access.

gap.description:
True when the consumer does not currently advertise this declaration's
intent, so the declaration is not being dispatched.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups the declaration covers.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

name.description: Operator-chosen display name for the declaration.

overdue_after.description:
Overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (e.g. `2h 30m` or `1d`):
how long the replica may go without a healthy restore report (or, for
at-most-once intents, how long the latest snapshot may go unverified)
before it is considered overdue. Null means no bound. The same format
is accepted back by `create` and `update`.

params.description:
Operator-supplied parameter values (name → value). Values of
`duration` and `bytes` parameters are formatted as human-friendly
strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) when the intent's schema is known;
`create` and `update` accept these strings back.

server_id.description:
Specific server within the group, or null to cover all current servers
in the group.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

updated_at.description: When the declaration was last modified.

RestoreReplicasCreateArgs.description:
Request to declare a new managed restore replica.

The consumer, group, server, backup type, and intent define the
declaration's scope; all of it can be changed later via `update`.

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device to assign the declaration to.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups to restore.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

name.description: Display name for the declaration.

overdue_after.description:
Overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (jiff's "friendly" format,
e.g. `2h 30m`, `36h`, `1d 12h`); omit, null, or blank for no bound.

params.description:
Parameter values for the intent (name → value), validated against the
consumer's advertised parameter schema. `duration` and `bytes`
parameters accept human-unit strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) as well
as raw integer seconds/bytes. Defaults to empty.

server_id.description:
Specific server within the group; omit or null to cover all current
servers in the group.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

Request to update an existing declaration.

Replaces every field, including scope: the consumer, group, server,
backup type, and intent can all be changed in the same call as the name,
overdue bound, parameter values, and enabled flag. A scope that collides
with another declaration's `(consumer, group, type, intent, server)` maps

consumer_device_id.description: Identifier of the restore consumer device to assign the declaration to.

enabled.description: Whether the declaration should be active.

group_id.description: Identifier of the server group whose backups to restore.

id.description: Identifier of the declaration to update.

intent.description:
How the replica is handled, as defined by the consumer: an arbitrary
identifier from the consumer's advertised intents, e.g. `verify`.

name.description: New display name for the declaration.

overdue_after.description:
New overdue bound as a human-friendly duration (jiff's "friendly"
format, e.g. `2h 30m`, `36h`, `1d 12h`); null or blank removes the
bound.

params.description:
New parameter values (name → value), validated against the intent's
advertised parameter schema. `duration` and `bytes` parameters accept
human-unit strings (e.g. `2h 30m`, `20Gi`) as well as raw integer
seconds/bytes. Defaults to empty.

server_id.description:
Specific server within the group; omit or null to cover all current
servers in the group.

type.description: The backup type to restore, for example `tamanu-postgres`.

RestoreWindowRow.description: A server's currently-open restore window, as shown in the group stats.

RetentionPolicy.description:
How many backups to keep at each retention tier once older snapshots are
pruned. The organization enforces minimum floors (at least 7 daily, 4
weekly, and 6 monthly) on write, unless the containing schedule or default
explicitly opts out via its `allow_below_floor` flag.

keep_annual.description:
Number of most-recent annual backups to keep. Defaults to 0 (no annual
retention).

keep_daily.description:
Number of most-recent daily backups to keep. Must be at least 7 unless
the retention floor is bypassed.

keep_latest.description:
Number of most-recent backups to always keep regardless of age.
Defaults to 1.

keep_monthly.description:
Number of most-recent monthly backups to keep. Must be at least 6
unless the retention floor is bypassed.

keep_weekly.description:
Number of most-recent weekly backups to keep. Must be at least 4 unless
the retention floor is bypassed.

entirely different fields.

Request body for creating a new snippet, or saving a new version of an
existing one.

description.description: Optional description of what the snippet does.

snippet with this id (an edit to an existing snippet). When
omitted, a brand new snippet is created.

Whether this override is allowed to fall below the organization's
minimum retention floor.

Expected seconds between scheduled backups of this type; null means
manual-only (no schedule), which is distinct from an interval of zero.

Retention policy override; null means inherit the canopy-wide default
for this backup type.

SelfAlertView.description:
A self-alert: a problem with canopy's own operation, such as an
expiring credential or a failed notification delivery — distinct from
issues raised against monitored servers.

Whether the underlying condition is still ongoing. Becomes `false`
once the condition has cleared on its own, independently of whether
an operator has resolved the alert.

effective_result.description: What policy made of it — the result canopy acts on.

escalates.description:
Whether this condition's policy escalates: an effective failure
notifies immediately, bypassing incident grace.

first_seen.description: When this condition was first raised.

last_seen.description: When this condition was most recently reaffirmed as still ongoing.

message.description: Full detail message describing the condition.

observed_result.description: What canopy observed on the latest raise, before policy.

ref.description:
The stable identifier of the underlying condition, e.g.
`mcp-token-expiry`. Stable across repeated raises of the same
condition.

resolved_at.description:
When an operator marked this alert resolved, or `null` if it has not
been resolved.

resolved_by.description:
The login of the operator who resolved this alert, or `null` if it
has not been resolved.

One backup type a server has advertised support for, whether the operator
has enabled it, and its most recent activity. Enabling a capability is
what makes the server eligible for issued backup credentials and
scheduled runs of that type.

enabled.description:
Whether the operator has enabled scheduled backups of this type for
this server.

latest_snapshot_bytes.description: Bytes uploaded by that run, if reported.

latest_snapshot_id.description:
Identifier of this server and type's most recent successful backup,
if any.

When this server's next backup of this type is expected: the server's own
last success plus the effective interval, or "now" (overdue) if it's
scheduled but has never succeeded. `None` for disabled or manual-only
(no-interval) types. Per-server, so a lagging member isn't masked by a
freshly-backed-up sibling.

`Some(issued_at)` when a backup of this type appears to be in flight:
backup credentials were issued and are still valid, and no run has
been reported since they were issued. `None` otherwise. Lets the UI
show a "backing up…" state.

Partial update to a server's fields. Only fields present in the request
are changed. For `device_id`, `group_id`, `public_name`, `cloud`, and
`geolocation`, sending an explicit `null` clears the field, while

New downtime threshold in seconds before this server is considered
down. Omit to leave unchanged.

device_id.description:
New device to bind to the server, or `null` to unbind. Omit to leave

to leave unchanged.

New URL for the server. An empty string clears it; omit to leave
unchanged.

Whether canopy should actively monitor this server. Omit to leave
unchanged.

notes.description: New free-text notes for the server. Omit to leave unchanged.

to leave unchanged.

Full detail view of a server: its own record, its bound device, its most
recent status report, current reachability/health, and group context.

billing_labels.description:
The server's effective `billing.*` labels — i.e. its group's
(product/deployment/stage). Empty when the server is ungrouped.

oneOf.description: Full detail on the device bound to this server, if any.

The group this server belongs to, with its notes/tags so the UI can
render the "Group" section without a second fetch. `None` when the
server is ungrouped.

health.description: Current self-reported health, derived from the most recent status report.

oneOf.description: The server's most recently reported status, if it has ever reported one.

siblings.description:
Other servers in the same group (excluding `server`). Empty when the
server is ungrouped or alone in its group. Each entry carries its
own `up` / `health` so the UI can render a status dot per sibling.

up.description: Current reachability, derived from the most recent status report.

ServerGroup.description:
A group of servers managed together: incidents roll up across the group,
members share tags, and the group carries its own notes and
notification settings.

deleted_at.description:
When set, the group is archived: hidden from live listings but kept,
along with its members, and can be restored.

oneOf.description:
The version reported by the group's canonical member server. `None`
if the group has no members or that member hasn't reported a
version yet.

name.description: The group's display name.

notes.description: Free-form operator notes about this group.

slack_close_delay.description:
How long, in seconds, an incident lingers after its last failure
recovers before it closes and the resolved notification is sent. A
failure returning within this window continues the same incident
instead of opening (and notifying about) a new one — the close-side
mirror of `slack_open_delay`, for a red check that briefly blips
green.

slack_open_delay.description:
How long, in seconds, an incident-opened notification waits before
it's sent. If the incident resolves within this window, the
notification is cancelled outright and never sent — useful for
groups prone to brief flapping, so a transient blip doesn't spam
notifications, without losing the underlying incident record.

tags.description: Key/value tags shared by every server in the group.

updated_at.description: When this group was last modified.

version_server_id.description:
The id of the group's canonical member server (the one whose version
is reflected in `effective_version`), chosen by highest rank then
highest kind. `None` when the group has no members.

ServerGroupCard.description:
A status-dashboard card summarising one group of equivalent servers, with
a status entry per member. The group's version is taken from whichever
member reported most recently.

members.description: Status of each server belonging to this group.

name.description: Name of the group.

oneOf.description:
Version reported by the most recently-reporting member of the group,
when known.

version_distance.description:
How far the reported `version` lags behind the latest known release,
when both are known. Combines the major and minor version gaps into a
single number that grows the further behind the version is (major
gaps count for more than minor ones); `0` means the version is
current or newer than the latest known release.

ServerGroupSilencedRef.description:
A silenced issue reference scoped to an entire server group: issues
matching this `(source, ref)` on any server in the group (or raised
directly against the group) are still recorded, but are excluded from
incidents and notifications.

created_by.description: The operator who created this silence. `None` if not recorded.

ref.description: The issue reference this silence matches.

server_group_id.description: The server group this silence applies to.

source.description: The issue source this silence matches.

name.description: Display name for the new group.

notes.description: Free-form notes about the group. Defaults to empty.

slack_close_delay.description:
Optional linger window, in whole seconds: how long an incident stays
open after its last failure recovers, so a failure returning within
the window continues the same incident instead of opening (and
notifying about) a new one. Omit to accept the default.

slack_open_delay.description:
Optional initial delay, in whole seconds, before an "incident opened"
Slack notification for this group is delivered; an incident that
resolves within the window never notifies. Omit to accept the default.

tags.description:
Tags to set on the group, as an object of string keys to string
values. Keys with the reserved `canopy:` prefix cannot be set.
Defaults to empty.

A server in the fleet inventory: its identity, classification, network
address, monitoring configuration, and (when requested by the endpoint)
current reachability/health.

alert_when_down_for.description:
Threshold in seconds for the reachability sweep to consider this
server down. Always positive; only consulted when `is_monitored`
is `true`. The default at creation is 600 (10 minutes).

cloud.description: Whether this server runs in a cloud environment, if known.

device_id.description: The device currently bound to this server, if any.

display_host.description:
